question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{x}^{2}-x+\frac{1}{4}.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-x+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}x+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=\frac{1}{2}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
